questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A businesswoman decided to destroy an old warehouse that she owned because the taxes on the structure exceeded the income that she could receive from it. She crept into the building in the middle of the night with a can of gasoline and a fuse and set the fuse timer for 30 minutes. She then left the building. The fuse failed to ignite, and the building was not harmed.
Arson is defined in this jurisdiction as "the intentional burning of any building or structure of another, without the consent of the owner." The businesswoman believed, however, that burning one's own building was arson, having been so advised by her lawyer.
Has the businesswoman committed attempted arson?

choices.A: No, because even if her actions had every consequence she intended, they would not have constituted arson.
choices.B: No, because her mistake negated a necessary mental state.
choices.C: Yes, because a mistake of law even on the advice of an attorney is no defense.
choices.D: Yes, because factual impossibility is no defense.

questions.explanation:
Defenses to attempt
Impossibility
  • Legal – intended act would not be criminal if completed
  • Factual (no defense) – unknown condition prevents completion of intended crime
Abandonment
  • Majority/common law (no defense) – attempt complete once overt act committed
  • Minority/MPC – voluntary & complete withdrawal from crime
MPC = Model Penal Code.
Attempt occurs when a person:
  • has the specific intent to commit a crime
  • performs an act in furtherance of the intended crime but
  • does not complete it.

Legal impossibility is a defense to attempt if the intended act would not be criminal even if completed.
That is because it is no crime to commit an act that is not a crime.

Here, the businesswoman decided to burn down her warehouse (specific intent). She crept into the warehouse with a can of gasoline and a fuse, then set a fuse timer (acts). However, the fuse did not ignite (incomplete crime). But even if she had successfully burned her warehouse, this jurisdiction limits arson to the intentional burning of another's building. Therefore, her attempted act would not have been criminal even if completed (legal impossibility).

(Choice B)  A defendant's honest but mistaken belief is a defense to specific intent crimes (eg, attempt) when that belief negates the specific intent (ie, mistake of fact). But since the businesswoman's mistaken belief did not prevent her from forming the specific intent to burn down her warehouse, it is not a defense here.

(Choice C)  Mistake or ignorance of the law is almost never a defense to criminal liability—even when a person relies on the advice of an attorney. But the businesswoman did not commit attempted arson because her intended act (even if completed) would not amount to arson in this jurisdiction.

(Choice D)  Factual impossibility arises when an unknown fact or circumstance prevents the defendant from completing the intended crime (eg, the malfunctioning fuse) and is never a defense to attempt. But legal impossibility (eg, burning one's building) is always a defense to attempt.

📌 Educational Objective

Legal impossibility is a defense to attempt when a person's intended act would not constitute a crime if completed.

一名女商人决定摧毁她所拥有的一座旧仓库，因为该建筑的税收超过了她能从中获得的收入。她在半夜带着一罐汽油和一根引信潜入该建筑，并将引信的定时器设置为30分钟。然后她离开了该建筑。引信未能点燃，建筑也未受损害。

在该司法管辖区，纵火罪（Arson）被定义为“未经所有者同意，故意焚烧他人的任何建筑物或构筑物。”然而，该女商人相信焚烧自己的建筑也构成纵火罪，因为她的律师是这样告知她的。

该女商人是否构成了纵火未遂罪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为即使她的行为产生了她所意图的所有后果，她的行为也不会构成纵火罪。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为她的错误排除了必要的犯罪意图（mental state）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法律上的错误，即使是基于律师的建议，也不能作为抗辩理由。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为事实不能（factual impossibility）不能作为抗辩理由。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Attempt

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：attempt（未遂）里，能不能用legal impossibility（法律不能完成）挡掉责任。

三秒认题路径：

故意放火 → 采取动作 → 题干法律定义 → 若完成也不犯罪 → 无未遂

核心法律规则

attempt（未遂）要求：有specific intent（特定故意），并且已经做了推动犯罪的行为，但最终没有完成。legal impossibility（法律不能完成）是抗辩：如果把行为真的做成了，也不会构成这个罪，那就不是可处罚的未遂。

这里题干把arson（纵火罪）定义成“烧another的建筑”，所以她就算真把自己仓库烧了，也不构成本辖区的 arson。她的错误是把“烧自己房子也算”当成了法律，但这不会把一个本来不违法的结果，硬变成未遂纵火。

核心判例： legal impossibility 逻辑和 attempt 的经典考法一致：如果完成后仍不犯罪，就没有可罚未遂。

思维导图

先问：她有没有 attempt 的基础结构？
1. 有 specific intent：她就是要把仓库烧掉。
2. 有 overt act：深夜潜入、带汽油、设引信。
3. 关键关卡：如果真的烧成，算不算 arson？
卡死点：不算。定义只罚“烧 another 的建筑”。
结论：这是 legal impossibility，所以不能定 attempted arson。
考试翻译：不是“没烧成所以无罪”，而是“就算烧成也不成罪，所以无未遂”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她带了汽油、点了引信、最后没烧成，听起来就是factual impossibility（事实不能完成）。

但考试真正问的是：如果她真的把仓库烧掉，法律会不会把这件事当作 arson。答案是不会，所以这不是事实障碍，而是法律障碍。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 就算成功烧成也不构成 arson，因为法条只罚烧“他人”建筑，所以她最多是想做一件在本辖区不算罪的事。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把她的belief当成会消灭故意，其实她的故意很明确。

❌ 法律适用 | 律师意见误套

✕ C: 误把律师建议当成挡箭牌，但这里关键不是咨询来源，而是完成后仍不成罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 不能完成偷换

✕ D: 把factual impossibility硬套上来，但题干的障碍来自法律定义，不是熔断的引信。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看法条定义，再问“完成后是否仍犯罪”，这一步一过就直接锁定 legal impossibility。

考场速记

Attempt（未遂）先看“有故意 + 有动作”，再问“完成后会不会还是犯罪”；如果答案是否，就记成 legal impossibility（法律不能完成）。

一句口诀：If completed but still not criminal, no attempt.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was angry at a coworker who had received a promotion. The man believed that the coworker had taken credit for the man's work and had bad-mouthed him to their boss. One day, as the man was leaving the company parking lot in his car, he saw the coworker walking through the lot. On a sudden impulse, the man pushed the accelerator pedal hard and veered toward the coworker with the intention of scaring him. The coworker tried to jump out of the way but slipped and fell and was run over. Although the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries, he survived.
In a jurisdiction that follows the common law of homicide, could the man properly be convicted of attempted murder?

choices.A: No, because the coworker's slip and fall broke the chain of proximate causation.
choices.B: No, because the man lacked the requisite intent.
choices.C: Yes, because the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries.
choices.D: Yes, because the man acted with reckless disregard for human life.

questions.explanation:
Malice aforethought

(attempted v. completed murder)
Attempted
murder
Completed
murder
Intent to kill
Conscious desire for, or substantial
certainty of, death
Intent to inflict serious bodily injury
Conscious desire for, or substantial certainty of,
serious bodily harm
Depraved-heart murder
Reckless disregard for high risk of death
or serious bodily harm
Felony murder
Killing during
inherently
dangerous felony

Attempt is an inchoate crime that requires proof that a defendant:

  • had the specific intent to commit a crime (eg, murder)
  • performed an overt act in furtherance of the intended crime but
  • did not complete it.

Therefore, attempted murder requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to kill the victim. This is true even though a completed murder can be established without showing an intent to kill—ie, when there is some other type of malice aforethought.

Here, the man cannot be convicted of attempted murder because he only intended to scare the coworker—not kill him. But had the coworker died, the man could have been convicted of murder since he acted with reckless disregard for human life (ie, malice aforethought) when he accelerated toward the coworker (Choice D).

(Choice A) Causation is relevant to crimes that require the occurrence of a particular result—eg, murder requires that the defendant cause the victim's death. But causation is irrelevant to attempt (and other inchoate crimes) since the intended result need not be completed. Therefore, the man is not guilty of attempted murder regardless of whether the coworker's slip and fall broke the chain of causation.

(Choice C) Although the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries, the man cannot be convicted of attempted murder since he lacked the specific intent to kill.

📌 Educational Objective

Attempt is a specific intent crime. Therefore, attempted murder requires proof that the defendant acted with the intent to kill—no other form of malice aforethought will suffice.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子对自己升职的同事感到愤怒。该男子认为同事抢了他的功劳，并在老板面前说他的坏话。一天，当该男子开车离开公司停车场时，他看到同事正穿过停车场。一时冲动之下，该男子猛踩油门，将车转向同事，意图吓唬他。同事试图跳开，但滑倒并被车碾过。虽然同事身受重伤，有生命危险，但他活了下来。

在一个遵循普通法杀人罪（homicide）的司法管辖区，该男子是否可以被正式定为谋杀未遂罪？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为同事的滑倒和摔倒中断了近因（proximate causation）的因果链。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该男子缺乏必要的意图。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为同事遭受了危及生命的伤害。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该男子的行为鲁莽，罔顾他人生命。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Attempt

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：attempt（未遂） 只看“有没有想杀”的特定故意，不看你后来有没有把人撞伤。

三秒认题路径：

想吓人 → 不是想杀人 → 未遂要特定故意 → 不能定 attempted murder → 选 B

核心法律规则

attempt（未遂） 是specific intent crime（特定故意犯罪），考场意思：必须证明被告就是想完成那个结果，不是“差不多、也许、很危险”就够了。

attempted murder（谋杀未遂） 必须证明被告有intent to kill（杀人故意），考场意思：reckless disregard、depraved-heart 这类“鲁莽到很坏”的心态，只能支撑完成后的 murder，不能替代未遂里的“我要杀”。

如果题干说他只是想吓人、不是想杀人，未遂就卡死；人最后受了重伤，也不能把“没有杀意”补成“有杀意”。

核心判例： common law 下的谋杀未遂逻辑就是这个：未遂看特定故意，不会因为结果很惨就自动补足杀人故意。

思维导图

看到“attempted murder”先问：他到底想要什么结果？
题干事实：他“故意向同事方向猛踩油门”，但明确是为了吓人，不是为了杀人。
第一关：attempt（未遂） 要特定故意。
卡死点：intent to kill（杀人故意） 不存在。
第二关：同事后来摔倒受重伤，不会把“想吓人”升级成“想杀人”。
结论：不能定 attempted murder，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然同事被撞成了 life-threatening injuries，那应该至少够重，能判 attempted murder。

但考试真正问的是：被告当时有没有想杀，不是后来伤得有多重。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题里更像“伤得很重的故意吓人”，不是“想杀人但没杀成”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的是他只想scare the coworker，不是想杀人；attempted murder 需要 intent to kill，所以不能定罪。

❌ 法律适用 | 因果关系误搬

✕ A: 把 chain of proximate causation 搬来；未遂不看结果链断不断。

❌ 事实误判 | 伤势严重偷换

✕ C: 看到 life-threatening injuries 就以为够了；重伤不等于杀人意图。

❌ 概念混淆 | 鲁莽当故意

✕ D: 把 reckless disregard 当成未遂所需的故意，层级错了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否是 specific intent，再问题干有没有把“想吓人”偷换成“想杀人”。

考场速记

记住一句：attempt 只认“我就是要做成”，不认“我只是很危险”。

碰到谋杀未遂，先找 intent to kill（杀人故意）；没有它，就别被重伤、恶意、鲁莽这些词带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was charged with felony murder because of his involvement in a bank robbery. The evidence at trial disclosed that a coworker invited the man to go for a ride in her new car, and after a while asked him to drive. As they drove around town, the coworker explained to the man that she planned to rob the bank and that she needed him to drive the getaway car. The man agreed to drive to the bank and to wait outside while the coworker went in to rob it.
As they approached the bank, the man began to regret his agreement to help with the robbery. Once there, the coworker got out of the car. As she went out of sight inside the bank, the man drove away and went home. Inside the bank, the coworker killed a bank guard who tried to prevent her from leaving with the money. The coworker ran outside and, finding that her car and the man were gone, ran down an alley. She was apprehended a few blocks away. The man later turned himself in after hearing on the radio that the coworker had killed the guard.
The jurisdiction has a death penalty that applies to felony murder.
Consistent with the law and the Constitution, of which crime may the jury convict the man?

choices.A: Felony murder and impose the death penalty.
choices.B: Felony murder but not impose the death penalty.
choices.C: Bank robbery only.
choices.D: No crime.

questions.explanation:
Accomplice liability & punishment for felony murder

Accomplice liability Did defendant intentionally aid/encourage
principal with intent that crime be completed?
No
Not guilty
Yes
Felony murder Did principal kill while committing inherently
dangerous felony encouraged by defendant?
No
Not guilty
Yes
Foreseeability Was murder natural & probable consequence
of encouraged crime?
No
Not guilty
Yes
Punishment Did defendant intend to kill or significantly &
recklessly participate in encouraged crime?
No
Guilty
(no death penalty)
Yes
Guilty
(death penalty)

Accomplice liability extends to any person who (1) intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime (2) with the specific intent that the crime be completed. Both parties are equally liable for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the man became an accomplice when he drove his coworker to the bank so that she could rob it. The man then fled the crime scene and did not encourage the commission of felony murder—the killing of another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony like robbery. But he is guilty of felony murder since the coworker killed a bank guard who tried to prevent her from taking the money—a foreseeable consequence of robbery (Choice D).

However, due to the Eighth Amendment prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment, the death penalty cannot be imposed on an accomplice to felony murder who did not kill or intend to kill—unless the accomplice significantly participated in the underlying felony and acted with reckless indifference to human life. And since the man merely dropped the coworker off at the bank, he did not significantly participate in the robbery. Therefore, the jury may convict him of felony murder but cannot impose the death penalty (Choice A).

(Choice C) In felony murder cases, the underlying felony is a lesser included offense that merges into the crime of felony murder. Therefore, a defendant can be convicted of either offense—but not both. So, though the man could be convicted of bank robbery (lesser offense), he will likely be convicted of felony murder (greater offense) instead.

📌 Educational Objective

The death penalty cannot be imposed on an accomplice to felony murder who did not kill or intend to kill—unless the accomplice (1) significantly participated in the felony and (2) acted with reckless indifference to human life.

📚 References
  • Enmund v. Florida, 458 U.S. 782, 790–91 (1982) (holding that the death penalty cannot be imposed on a felony-murder accomplice who did not kill or intend to kill).
  • Tison v. Arizona, 481 U.S. 137, 158 (1987) (imposing the death penalty on a felony-murder accomplice who was a major participant in the underlying felony and acted with reckless indifference to human life).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因参与银行抢劫而被控重罪谋杀（felony murder）。庭审证据显示，一名同事邀请该男子乘坐她的新车，过了一会儿，同事让该男子开车。当他们在城里开车时，同事向该男子解释说，她计划抢劫银行，并需要他来开逃逸车辆。该男子同意开车到银行，并在同事进去抢劫时在外面等候。

当他们接近银行时，该男子开始后悔自己同意协助抢劫。到达银行后，同事下了车。在该同事进入银行，离开他的视线后，该男子开车离开并回了家。在银行内，同事杀死了一名试图阻止她带钱离开的银行警卫。同事跑到外面，发现她的车和该男子都不见了，于是跑进一条小巷。她在几个街区外被逮捕。该男子后来在收音机里听到同事杀害了警卫的消息后自首。

该司法管辖区对重罪谋杀适用死刑。

根据法律和宪法，陪审团可以判定该男子犯有何种罪行？

zh-choices.A: 重罪谋杀，并处以死刑。
zh-choices.B: 重罪谋杀，但不处以死刑。
zh-choices.C: 仅银行抢劫罪。
zh-choices.D: 无罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：帮同伙抢劫的 共犯（accomplice） 是否会被判 felony murder，以及他能不能被判死刑。

三秒认题路径：

先看共犯 → 再看杀人 → 再看可预见 → 最后看死刑

核心法律规则

如果你是 共犯（accomplice），先问你有没有故意帮助或鼓励主犯，并且希望犯罪完成；有的话，你要为该犯罪及其自然、可预见后果负责。这里的 felony murder 考的是抢劫过程中是否发生了可预见的致死结果，所以他可以被判该罪。

但 死刑（death penalty） 还要额外过一关：共犯本人通常必须杀人、想杀人，或者至少在基础重罪里是重大参与者并对人命有 reckless indifference。只是在门口当接应、后来又跑掉，通常不够。

核心判例： Enmund v. Florida 限制对未杀人、未意图杀人的 felony-murder 共犯判死刑；Tison v. Arizona 说明只有“重大参与 + 对生命漠视”才可能跨过这道门。

思维导图

先看：他是不是 accomplice？
YES：明知对方要抢银行，还主动帮忙开车、接送，说明他是故意帮助者。
再看：主犯在抢劫中是否杀了人？
YES：银行守卫被杀，且死在抢劫进行时，进入 felony murder。
第三关：这次杀人是不是抢劫的自然可预见后果？
YES：抢劫里遇到阻拦、守卫被杀，很容易预见。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 不是这里的重点；本题的死穴在死刑门槛。
最后看：他能不能被判死刑？
NO：他没有亲手杀人，也没有证据显示他是重大参与者到足以满足 reckless indifference。
结论：可判 felony murder，但不能判死刑。
一句话记：帮忙抢劫 → 可能背 felony murder；但没杀人、没到重大参与，死刑通常卡掉。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他后来临阵反悔，还开车跑了，所以连 felony murder 也不该算在他头上。

但考试真正问的是：他前面已经故意帮忙，主犯随后在抢劫中杀人，这个死亡是不是帮抢劫的可预见后果。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同理，后悔或逃走不自动切断已经成立的共犯责任。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 明知抢银行仍去接应，足以成立共犯并承担抢劫引发的 felony murder；但他没有杀人，也不是重大参与者，死刑门槛没过。

❌ 事实误判 | 退场切断误读

✕ A: 把他后来的离开当成自动免责，忽略前面已完成的共犯帮助。

❌ 法律适用 | 罪名合并误判

✕ C: 以为只剩 bank robbery，忘了抢劫中的致死结果会把案子推到 felony murder。

❌ 概念混淆 | 事后反悔混同

✕ D: 把“后来投案”当成没犯罪，但事后自首不抹掉前面的故意帮助。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定共犯成立，再问重罪致死，最后单独检查死刑门槛。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Enmund 卡“没杀人、没想杀人”；Tison 才给“重大参与 + 对生命漠视”留门。看到共犯型 felony murder，先判罪名，再单独判死刑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman and her sister took a trip to the Caribbean. When they passed through U.S. Customs inspection upon their return, the customs officials found packages of cocaine stitched inside separate carry-on bags belonging to each of them. They were arrested. Upon separate questioning by customs officers, the woman broke down and cried, "I told my sister there were too many officers at this airport." The sister did not give a statement.
The woman and her sister were indicted for conspiracy to import cocaine. They were tried separately. At the woman's trial, after the government introduced the above evidence and rested its case, her lawyer moved for a judgment of acquittal on grounds of insufficient evidence.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because the evidence shows that both the woman and her sister agreed to import cocaine.
choices.B: No, because the evidence shows that both the woman and her sister possessed cocaine.
choices.C: Yes, because the evidence shows only that the woman and her sister committed separate crimes of cocaine possession.
choices.D: Yes, because the evidence shows that the woman effectively withdrew from the conspiracy when she cooperated by giving a statement.

questions.explanation:
Conspiracy
Agreement Overt act
Majority view
(modern & MPC)		 Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement At least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view
(common law)		 Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement Not required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Conspiracy requires proof that:

  • two or more persons entered an agreement (explicitly or implicitly) with the specific intent to commit a crime* and
  • in most jurisdictions, at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of that agreement.

Therefore, a court should grant a motion for acquittal if no rational trier of fact could find that the evidence, viewed in the light most favorable to the prosecution, establishes these elements beyond a reasonable doubt.

Here, there is no evidence of an explicit agreement (eg, express words). But a rational trier of fact could find evidence of an implicit agreement because (1) the statement that "I told my sister there were too many officers at this airport" and (2) the cocaine found inside the sisters' carry-on bags show their intent to jointly achieve a criminal objective—importing cocaine. Therefore, the court should deny the woman's motion for acquittal.

*Whether this jurisdiction follows the unilateral or bilateral approach to conspiracy is not stated. However, there is evidence that both women agreed and specifically intended to import cocaine, so either approach is satisfied under these facts.

(Choice B) Evidence that the sisters possessed cocaine also shows that they committed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy. But since an overt act is not an element of conspiracy in every jurisdiction, this is not the strongest basis for denying the woman's motion.

(Choice C) The evidence shows that the woman and her sister committed separate crimes of cocaine possession. But it also shows that they committed conspiracy—a distinct crime.

(Choice D) Withdrawal is only a defense to conspiracy after an overt act under the Model Penal Code, which requires that the defendant voluntarily renounce the conspiracy and thwart its success. Here, the woman's statement to customs officers did not prevent the import of cocaine, so she did not withdraw.

📌 Educational Objective

Conspiracy requires an agreement between two persons to commit a crime, but the agreement need not be express. It can be implied from conduct demonstrating an intent to jointly achieve a shared criminal objective.
questions.zh-question:
一名女子和她的妹妹去加勒比地区旅行。当她们返回并通过U.S. Customs（美国海关）检查时，海关官员在她们各自的随身行李中发现了缝在里面的可卡因包裹。她们被逮捕了。在海关官员的分别讯问下，该女子崩溃大哭道：‘我告诉过我妹妹这个机场的官员太多了。’妹妹没有作出任何陈述。

该女子和她的妹妹因共谋进口可卡因而被起诉。她们被分案审理。在该女子的审判中，政府在提交了上述证据并结束其陈述后，她的律师以证据不足为由，请求作出无罪判决。

法院是否应批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为证据表明该女子和她的妹妹都同意进口可卡因。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为证据表明该女子和她的妹妹都持有可卡因。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为证据仅表明该女子和她的妹妹分别犯有持有可卡因的罪行。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为证据表明该女子通过合作作出陈述，有效地退出了共谋。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Conspiracy

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共谋（conspiracy）不要求明说，只要题干事实足以让陪审团看出双方有共同的犯罪目标和默契配合，就能否定无罪裁定。

三秒认题路径：

共同运毒 → 看默契 → 找暗示同意 → 不是单纯持有 → 不能无罪

核心法律规则

共谋（conspiracy）的核心是：至少两个人就犯罪目标达成了协议（agreement），这个协议可以是明说的，也可以从行为里推出来。考试上你要盯住的是，题干有没有足够事实让理性陪审团看出双方想一起完成同一个非法目标。

明示同意（express agreement）不是必须；默示同意（implicit agreement）也够用。多数法域还要求一个外部行为（overt act），但这题真正先过的是“有没有 agreement”这道门。

核心判例： MPC 的思路和多数法域一致地承认：只要有共同犯罪意图，协议可由事实推断，不必等到嘴上说“我们一起干”。

思维导图

先看：题干有没有agreement？
YES姐妹同去加勒比海，回程每人的背包里都缝着可卡因，说明不是单人单干，而是一起运毒。
再看：有没有直接说“我们约好一起进口”？
没有明说也没关系；implicit agreement 可以从“我告诉我妹妹机场人太多了”+ 双方各自携毒推出来。
最后问：理性陪审团能不能据此认定双方都想共同进口可卡因？
能 → 共谋成立 → 不能因为“只有单独持有”就放人。
NO如果只有各自持有、没有共同目标线索，才会掉进“只是两个独立犯罪”的坑。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这不就是两个人各自藏毒，所以只是separate crimes。

但考试真正问的是：有没有证据显示她们在做同一件事、而不是各玩各的。

司法考试看的是「是否能推到共同协议」，不是只看表面上是不是每个人各自拿着一包毒品。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里的 “I told my sister…” 加上两人各自携毒，足够让陪审团推断她们有共同进口可卡因的默示协议，所以不能判无罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 持有当协议

✕ B: 只看到 possessed cocaine，把“有毒品”误当成“有共谋”。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看持有罪

✕ C: 把题目缩成单纯持有，漏掉了共同进口的协同行为线索。

❌ 法律适用 | 退群规则搬错

✕ D: withdrew 不是这里的救命按钮；她只是对海关哭诉，并没有真正瓦解共谋。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找共同目标线索，再判断是不是能从事实推成默示 agreement；别被“各自持有”带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：共谋先看协议，不看嘴硬。有共同犯罪目标的事实线索，就能把“没明说”变成“已同意”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An undercover police detective told a local drug dealer that she wanted to buy cocaine but needed time to raise the necessary funds. The drug dealer said that he needed time to get the cocaine. They agreed to meet again in 10 days. An hour later, without a warrant, other officers forcibly entered the drug dealer's apartment and arrested him for attempted possession of a controlled substance.
If the drug dealer is prosecuted in a common law jurisdiction for attempted possession of cocaine, should he be convicted?

choices.A: No, because he had not taken sufficient steps toward commission of the crime.
choices.B: No, because he was illegally arrested.
choices.C: Yes, because by objective standards the undercover detective and the drug dealer had made an agreement that the dealer would obtain cocaine.
choices.D: Yes, because he unequivocally expressed his intent to obtain the cocaine.

questions.explanation:
Attempt
(inchoate crime)
Mens rea
(specific intent) 		Actus reus
(overt act)
Common law Intends to commit
target offense		 Dangerous-proximity test – performs act sufficiently close to completing target offense
Majority & MPC Substantial-step test – engages in conduct that exceeds mere preparation & strongly corroborates criminal intent
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Criminal liability for an attempted crime arises when a defendant:

  • has the specific intent to commit a crime
  • performs an overt act in furtherance of the target crime but
  • does not complete it.

An overt act must go beyond mere preparation for the target crime. At common law, this requires the defendant to perform an act that is sufficiently close—in time and physical proximity—to completing the target crime (ie, dangerous proximity test). In other words, the defendant must commit an act that is indispensable to the crime's success.

Here, the drug dealer was charged with attempted possession of cocaine because he told the undercover detective that he needed time to get cocaine for her to buy. The drug dealer's statement evidences his intent to obtain cocaine. But this interaction did not amount to an overt act because it did not bring the drug dealer dangerously close to completing the crime—especially since he and the detective were not going to meet again for 10 days (Choice D). Therefore, the drug dealer should not be convicted.

(Choice B) While an illegal (eg, warrantless) arrest may lead to suppression of evidence, it will not stop a criminal prosecution or serve as a defense to the charged crime. Therefore, the dealer could be convicted despite being illegally arrested.

(Choice C) Merely agreeing to commit a crime is not an overt act under either the dangerous proximity test (common law approach) or substantial step test (modern approach).

📌 Educational Objective

Attempt requires proof that the defendant committed an overt act in furtherance of the intended crime. At common law, this requirement is met when the defendant performs an act that is dangerously close (in time and physical proximity) to completing the intended crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名卧底警探告诉当地一名毒贩，她想购买可卡因，但需要时间筹集必要的资金。该毒贩说他需要时间去获取可卡因。他们同意在10天后再次会面。一小时后，在没有搜查令的情况下，其他警员强行进入该毒贩的公寓，并以未遂持有受管制物品罪逮捕了他。

如果该毒贩在普通法司法管辖区因未遂持有可卡因罪被起诉，他是否应被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为他尚未为实施犯罪采取足够的步骤。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为他被非法逮捕。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为根据客观标准，卧底警探和毒贩已达成协议，由毒贩获取可卡因。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为他明确表达了获取可卡因的意图。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Attempt

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：attempt（未遂）在普通法下是否已经走到超出单纯准备的那一步。

三秒认题路径：

特定故意 → 超出准备 → 危险接近 → 还没到位 → 选 A

核心法律规则

做题只抓这条线

attempt（未遂）必须同时有specific intent（特定故意）和overt act（外部行为）；考场意思：光想做不够，必须已经开始往犯罪结果推进。

在common law（普通法）下，外部行为要达到dangerous-proximity test（危险接近标准）；考场意思：动作要离既遂很近，近到几乎就是最后一步。

这里更像是“约好以后再交易”，还不是“已经把毒品推进到眼前”；所以只是准备，不是未遂。

核心判例：Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题真正锁定的是未遂的危险接近标准，不是上诉可立即性。

思维导图

先问：被告有没有 specific intent（特定故意）？
有：他说“需要时间去弄到可卡因”，说明想取得毒品。
再问：有没有 overt act（外部行为），而且超出 mere preparation（单纯准备）？
没有：只是说还要时间、约 10 天后再见，没有把犯罪推进到最后一步。
卡死点：没有危险接近（dangerous proximity），所以还不是未遂。
结论：普通法未遂要“想 + 做到很近”，本题只做到“想”。
答案：选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他已经明确说要去弄可卡因，还跟警探约了时间，应该算开始实施了。

但考试真正问的是：这一步有没有把犯罪推到足够接近完成，而不是有没有表现出犯罪念头。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干只有“要去找毒品”和“10 天后再见”，还没把可卡因推进到危险接近，所以不足以成立未遂。

❌ 事实误判 | 非法逮捕误导

✕ B: 把illegal arrest当成抗辩理由了，逮捕违法不等于未遂成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 协议即未遂误判

✕ C: 以为“双方谈妥”就够了，但单纯 agreement 还是准备，不是外部实行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 意图当行为

✕ D: 他说得很明确，unequivocally 只是证明故意，不是证明已开始实施。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“想做”还是“已经做得很近”，故意和外部行为要分开看。

考场速记

记住：attempt（未遂）不是“说想做”，而是“已经做到离完成很近”。看到只是约时间、等资金、下次再说，先想单纯准备，别急着选未遂。

口诀：Specific intent + overt act，再看有没有越过 mere preparation；普通法下还要问一句：是不是已经 dangerously close。

reason.zh: 表明本题考察的未遂犯罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was planning to propose to his girlfriend, so he took her to a jewelry store to look at engagement rings. After trying on several rings, the girlfriend selected a ring that was well outside of the man's price range. The man asked the girlfriend to wait in the car while he purchased the ring. Once she exited the jewelry store, the man pulled out a gun and robbed the store.
After the robbery, the man calmly returned to the car and sat silently as the girlfriend unwittingly drove them to their house. Shortly after their arrival, a police officer knocked on their front door. Panicked, the man told the girlfriend that he had robbed the jewelry store and begged her not to open the door. Despite his pleas, the girlfriend answered the door. The man quickly hid inside their bedroom closet. When the officer asked the girlfriend where the man was, she said that the man was headed to a neighboring town. The girlfriend provided no further information to the police.
If the woman is charged as an accessory after the fact to robbery and the above evidence is presented at trial, which verdict should the jury render?

choices.A: Guilty, because the girlfriend aided the man by driving the getaway car.
choices.B: Guilty, because the girlfriend told the police officer that the man was headed to a neighboring town.
choices.C: Not guilty, because the girlfriend did not learn of the robbery until after its commission.
choices.D: Not guilty, because the girlfriend had no duty to report the robbery to the police.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
Modern view Common law Definition Liability
Principal Principal
(first degree)		 Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act Target &
foreseeable
crimes
Accomplice Principal
(second degree)		 Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
before the fact*		 Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
after the fact		 Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction Independent
crime
*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

A person is an accessory after the fact if he/she:

  • knew that the principal had committed a felony
  • aided or assisted the principal after the felony was committed and
  • did so for the specific purpose of helping the principal avoid apprehension or conviction.

As a result, a person who gives false information to the police to prevent the apprehension of a felon is an accessory after the fact. But a person who merely fails to report a crime is generally not.

Here, the girlfriend learned that the man had committed a felony after he told her that he had robbed the jewelry store. And though the girlfriend had no duty to report the robbery upon learning about it, she gave the police false information—that the man was headed to a neighboring town—to help him avoid apprehension (Choice D). Therefore, the jury should find the girlfriend guilty as an accessory after the fact to robbery.

(Choice A) The girlfriend may have aided the man by driving him away from the robbery. But at that time, she did not know that the man had committed the robbery. Therefore, this fact is insufficient to find the girlfriend guilty as an accessory after the fact.

(Choice C) The girlfriend did not learn of the robbery until after its commission. But upon learning of it, she lied to the police for the specific purpose of helping the man avoid arrest and is therefore an accessory after the fact.

📌 Educational Objective

An accessory after the fact is someone who knows that a person committed a felony and aids that person for the purpose of helping him/her avoid apprehension or conviction. One can be convicted as an accessory after the fact for giving the police false information to prevent apprehension of a felon, but not for merely failing to report a crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子正计划向女友求婚，因此带她去了一家珠宝店看订婚戒指。在试戴了几枚戒指后，女友选中了一枚远超该男子价格预算的戒指。该男子让女友在车里等他，他去购买戒指。待女友离开珠宝店后，该男子掏出枪抢劫了商店。

抢劫后，该男子冷静地回到车里，在女友不知情地开车将他们载回家时，他一言不发。他们抵达后不久，一名警察敲响了他们家的前门。该男子惊慌失措，告诉女友他抢劫了珠宝店，并恳求她不要开门。尽管他再三恳求，女友还是开了门。该男子迅速躲进卧室的衣柜里。当警察问女友该男子在哪里时，她说该男子已前往邻近的城镇。女友没有向警方提供任何进一步的信息。

如果该女子被指控为抢劫案的事后从犯，并且上述证据在审判中被呈示，陪审团应作出何种裁决？

zh-choices.A: 有罪，因为女友驾驶逃逸车辆帮助了该男子。
zh-choices.B: 有罪，因为女友告诉警察该男子已前往邻近的城镇。
zh-choices.C: 无罪，因为女友直到抢劫案发生后才知情。
zh-choices.D: 无罪，因为女友没有义务向警方报告抢劫案。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：事后帮凶（accessory after the fact）是不是已经知道对方重罪成立后，再用假话帮他躲警察；单纯没报警不够，说谎误导警方才会中招。

三秒认题路径：

先知其罪 → 事后帮忙 → 为躲追捕 → 假话给警察 → 有罪

核心法律规则

事后帮凶（accessory after the fact）要满足三步：先知道对方已经犯了重罪（felony），再在犯罪完成后提供帮助，最后目的必须是帮他躲逮捕或定罪（avoid apprehension or conviction）。考试里最常见的帮助形式，就是对警方提供虚假信息（false information）。单纯不举报（mere failure to report）一般不够定罪。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题锁定的是普通刑法里的事后帮凶规则：知道重罪后再用谎言帮人逃避追捕，就成立。

思维导图

先看：她是在犯罪前帮忙，还是在犯罪后帮忙？
① 先前帮忙？陪去珠宝店、开车离开，这些都发生在她知道抢劫之前。
卡死点：不知道已犯重罪时，不能算事后帮凶。
② 事后帮忙？男方已经坦白抢劫后，她对警察说他“去了邻镇”。
卡死点：这不是沉默，而是故意误导警方，正好命中 accessory after the fact。
③ 结论不看她有没有义务举报，只看她有没有在知情后用假话帮人躲抓捕。
答案：B 有罪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她只是没报警，或者只是开车带他回家，所以不算帮凶。

但考试真正问的是：她在知道抢劫已经发生后，有没有故意帮他躲警察。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

她已知道男方抢劫后，仍对警察说他去了邻镇，这是典型的知情后用假话帮其逃避追捕，所以成立 accessory after the fact。

❌ 事实误判 | 先前帮忙偷换

✕ A: 把driving the getaway car当成知情后帮凶，但她当时还不知道抢劫。

❌ 概念混淆 | 知情时间误判

✕ C: 盯着after its commission却忽略她后来已经开始替他撒谎。

❌ 法律适用 | 不报案误当无罪

✕ D: 把duty to report当核心，但本题不是不报案，而是主动误导警方。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓时间点：先知情、后帮忙、且是帮他逃避追捕，最后再判断是不是只是沉默还是已经说谎。

考场速记

记住一句话：知道重罪 + 事后帮忙 + 目的在躲抓捕，才是 accessory after the fact；不举报通常不够，对警方说假话才是高频陷阱。

reason.en: Defines the specific charge and its required elements the jury must evaluate.
reason.zh: 界定被告被指控的罪名及陪审团必须审查的要件。

reason.en: The principal must have committed a felony for accessory after the fact liability to attach.

keywords.text: unwittingly drove them to their house

reason.zh: 驾车时女友不知情，故该行为不构成事后从犯责任。

reason.zh: 表明女友在向警方陈述前已获悉重罪，知情要件因此满足。

reason.en: She drove without knowledge of the felony, so this act cannot satisfy the knowledge element of accessory after the fact.

B.text: told the police officer that the man was headed to a neighboring town

C.text: did not learn of the robbery until after its commission

reason.zh: 虽属实但无关紧要；事后从犯要求的是事后知情，而非事前知情。

D.text: no duty to report the robbery

reason.en: Correct as a general principle but irrelevant here because the girlfriend did more than fail to report—she actively lied.

reason.en: This active lie to police, made with knowledge of the felony, is the act that constitutes accessory after the fact.

highlights.text: he had robbed the jewelry store

reason.en: This is the moment the girlfriend gained knowledge of the felony, satisfying the first element of accessory after the fact.
reason.zh: 这是女友获悉重罪的时刻，满足事后从犯的知情要件。

highlights.text: unwittingly drove them to their house

reason.en: Establishes she lacked knowledge during the drive, making choice A incorrect.
reason.zh: 证明驾车时她尚不知情，使选项A不成立。

highlights.text: accessory after the fact to robbery

reason.en: Frames the legal question: does the girlfriend's conduct meet all elements of this specific charge?

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man decided to steal a valuable coin collection from a collector's house while the collector was away. Knowing that the house had an alarm system, the man contacted the pool cleaner who worked at the house twice a week. The man offered the pool cleaner part of the proceeds from selling the coin collection if she would disarm the alarm and leave a side door unlocked so that the man could enter the house. The pool cleaner pretended to agree but then contacted the police, who immediately arrested the man.
In a jurisdiction that follows the common law and has adopted the bilateral requirement for conspiracy, what crime has the man committed?

choices.A: Attempted burglary.
choices.B: Attempted larceny.
choices.C: Conspiracy.
choices.D: Solicitation.

questions.explanation:
Inchoate crimes
Attempt
  • Specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of target crime
  • Merges with intended crime if completed
Conspiracy
  • Agreement entered with specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of agreement
  • No merger
Solicitation
  • Inducing or encouraging another to commit crime with specific intent that crime be committed, but solicited party need not agree
  • Merges with solicited crime if completed

At common law (and in most jurisdictions), solicitation is an inchoate offense that requires proof that the defendant:

  • enticed, encouraged, or commanded another to commit a crime (eg, burglary or larceny)
  • with the specific intent that the person commit that crime.

Here, the man enticed the pool cleaner to help him steal the coin collection from the collector's house by offering to share proceeds from selling the collection with her. And the man specifically intended that the pool cleaner help him steal the coins by disarming the alarm and leaving a side door unlocked. Therefore, he committed solicitation.

(Choices A & B) Attempt occurs when a defendant (1) has the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) commits an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) does not complete it. In this common law jurisdiction, an act must bring the defendant sufficiently close to completing the target offense. Therefore, mere preparation (eg, soliciting help to commit a crime) is not enough.

(Choice C) Conspiracy occurs when two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime. The common law bilateral theory of conspiracy requires proof of at least two guilty minds—the defendant and one other conspirator. Therefore, a defendant cannot be convicted when the only other conspirator feigns agreement (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Common law solicitation occurs when a defendant (1) entices, encourages, or commands another to commit a crime (2) with the specific intent that the person commit the crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定在收藏家外出时从其家中盗窃一套贵重的钱币收藏品。该男子知道房子里有警报系统，于是联系了每周在房子里工作两次的泳池清洁工。该男子向泳池清洁工提出，如果她能解除警报并留下一扇侧门不上锁，以便该男子进入房屋，他将分给她一部分出售钱币收藏品的收益。泳池清洁工假装同意，但随后联系了警方，警方立即逮捕了该男子。

在一个遵循普通法并采纳了共谋罪双边要求的司法管辖区，该男子犯了什么罪？

zh-choices.A: 入室盗窃未遂罪。
zh-choices.B: 盗窃罪未遂。
zh-choices.C: 共谋罪。
zh-choices.D: 教唆罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Solicitation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告只是怂恿/诱使（solicitation）他人帮自己去犯罪，还没形成双方的有效合意，所以不是共谋（conspiracy），也不是未遂（attempt）。

三秒认题路径：

诱使他人 → 别人假装同意 → 没有双边合意 → 不是共谋 → 选 solicitation

核心法律规则

Solicitation（教唆/怂恿犯罪） 的考场意思：你只要有specific intent（特定故意）去让对方犯罪，并且去诱使、鼓励或命令对方犯罪，就已经成立；对方不需要真的答应。

Conspiracy（共谋） 的考场意思：必须有双方都真的想犯罪的agreement（合意）；在双边主义（bilateral requirement）下，只有一边真想、一边假装配合，不算共谋。

Attempt（未遂） 的考场意思：光开口找人帮忙还不够，必须已经有足够接近完成犯罪的实行行为；单纯拉人下水还是停在前置阶段。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题不是上诉法，而是普通法下的未完成犯区分，关键在于“诱使”本身就够成罪。

思维导图

先看：被告是在“拉人一起犯罪”，还是已经“往完成犯罪推进”了？
第一关
有双方真实合意吗？
没有对方只是假装同意，双边共谋卡死。
卡死点：agreement 不成立 → 不是 conspiracy
第二关
被告有没有只是在诱使别人去犯罪？
有提出分赃、要求开门、让人关警报，已经是在encourage / entice。
卡死点：只要有特定故意 + 诱使他人犯罪 → 直接落入 solicitation
第三关
有没有已经接近偷到手？
没有。还停在找人配合的阶段，mere preparation（单纯准备） 不够。
卡死点：未到实行行为 → 不是 attempt
结论：选 Solicitation，因为“诱使”本身就成立；“假装答应”只会打掉 conspiracy。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方都按他说的去做了，还差点开门放他进去，所以应该是attempt 或 conspiracy。

但考试真正问的是：被告此时只是把别人往犯罪方向推，真正的双边合意根本没成立；而且他还没走到足够接近完成盗窃的那一步。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上/构成要件上能不能成立该罪」，而不是「物理上有没有差点得手」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里他主动提出分赃、要求对方关警报和开侧门，已经是在诱使他人去犯罪；对方是否真心同意不影响 solicitation 成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 直接跳未遂

✕ A: 把attempted burglary想得太早了，光找人配合还没到“足够接近完成”。

❌ 事实误判 | 偷换实行行为

✕ B: 题干没有他已经去撬门或搬运赃物，attempted larceny 还差一步。

❌ 概念混淆 | 双边合意误读

✕ C: bilateral requirement 下，对方假装配合就不是共谋。

这题建议用什么方法？

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man and a woman were partners in an automobile leasing agency. For some time, the man had been embezzling money from the agency. The woman became suspicious and told the man that she wanted to engage an accounting firm to audit the agency's books. In a panic to prevent the audit and avoid being discovered, the man decided to have the woman killed. He contacted a professional killer and hired him to kill the woman for $10,000. A short time later, the woman died in a car crash arranged by the killer.
In addition to embezzlement, of what crime or crimes may the man properly be convicted?

choices.A: Conspiracy and murder.
choices.B: Murder.
choices.C: Solicitation and conspiracy.
choices.D: Solicitation, conspiracy, and murder.

questions.explanation:
Merger of inchoate & completed crimes
Attempt
Merger
Completed crime
Solicitation
Merger
Completed crime
Conspiracy
No merger
Completed crime

A person who unlawfully kills another with malice aforethought is principally liable for murder. But a person who did not commit that killing is equally liable for murder if he/she acted as an accomplice by (1) intentionally aiding or encouraging the principal before or during the crime (2) with the specific intent that the crime be completed. As a result, a person can become an accomplice when he/she commits either:

  • solicitation – by inducing or encouraging another to commit a crime with the specific intent that the crime be committed or
  • conspiracy – by entering an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and, in most jurisdictions, at least one conspirator committing an overt act in furtherance of that agreement.

Here, the man committed solicitation and conspiracy when he contacted and hired a professional killer to kill the woman—subjecting the man to accomplice liability. And since the killer successfully arranged the deadly car crash pursuant to their agreement, the man can be convicted of murder (Choice B). And though he cannot be convicted of solicitation since it merges with the solicited crime once completed (Choices C & D), he can still be convicted of conspiracy since it remains a separate offense.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who commits solicitation or conspiracy is often subject to accomplice liability for the encouraged crime. And if the encouraged crime is completed, the defendant can be convicted of the completed crime and conspiracy—but not solicitation since it merges with the completed crime.

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Solicitation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：solicitation（教唆）在被教唆的谋杀已经完成后会与既遂犯罪merge（并入），但conspiracy（共谋）不会并入，所以能判共谋和谋杀，不能再判教唆。

三秒认题路径：

叫人杀人 → 杀人成功 → 看并入 → 教唆消失 → 共谋保留

核心法律规则

solicitation（教唆）的考场意思：诱使别人去犯罪，本身就够成立，但一旦被教唆的犯罪真的做成了，教唆通常会merge（并入）到既遂罪里，所以不能再单独定教唆。

conspiracy（共谋）的考场意思：只要有合意加上通常所需的行为推进，它就是独立罪名；即使后面把事做成了，共谋一般也还在。

如果行为人还主动请人去杀人，他也会因为帮助或促成既遂杀人而承担accomplice liability（共犯责任），所以最后可以落到谋杀和共谋。

核心判例：本题对应 merger 逻辑：教唆遇到既遂罪会并入，但共谋不会并入，所以最终能判共谋和既遂谋杀。

思维导图

先问：有没有把“叫人杀她”真的做成？
有 教唆（solicitation）并入既遂谋杀，不能再单独定教唆
还有 是否只是合意＋推进？
是 共谋（conspiracy）不并入，继续成立
结果 谋杀 + 共谋
卡死点 别把“教唆完成了”误当成还能再单独加一项

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他一开始就找杀手、出钱、安排杀人，那教唆和共谋不是都能保留吗。

但考试真正问的是：被教唆的杀人已经完成后，教唆会不会被并入；答案是会，所以不能再单独定 solicitation。

这里不是看他“做没做坏事很多次”，而是看哪一项是独立保留、哪一项会被既遂罪吞掉。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里他联系并雇用杀手，先成立conspiracy；而杀人已经做成，所以最终可定谋杀加共谋，solicitation（教唆）则并入既遂罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略共谋

✕ B: 只看到结果是杀人，漏掉前面的hired him和合意。

❌ 法律适用 | 并入规则错放

✕ C: 把共谋也当成会并入的罪，错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把教唆当独立保留

✕ D: 以为教唆、共谋、谋杀能全留，但merges已经把教唆吃掉了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“完成了没有”再看并入：完成的既遂罪保留，教唆消失，共谋继续。

考场速记

记住一句：教唆会并入，共谋不并入；看到“叫人去做”且事情真的做成了，先保留既遂罪和共谋，再删掉教唆。

这题的快捷判断就是：solicitation + completed crime = merge，conspiracy + completed crime = still there。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:
CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.
CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.
CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.
CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes let his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.
A plastic surgeon agreed to remove the fingerprints from the hands of a man whom the surgeon knew to be a safecracker. The surgeon charged his usual hourly rate for the operation. Afterward, the man burglarized a bank safe and was convicted of burglary. The surgeon has been charged with burglary.
Should he be convicted or acquitted of this crime?

choices.A: Convicted on the authority of Case A.
choices.B: Convicted on the authority of Case B.
choices.C: Acquitted on the authority of Case C.
choices.D: Acquitted on the authority of Case D.

questions.explanation:
Inferred intent for accomplice liability

Unusually large profit from sale
Highly specialized goods or services
I’m gonna
rob a bank.
Then that’ll be
double the price.

Although the surgeon did not commit burglary, he can be convicted under the theory of accomplice liability if he:

  • intentionally aided or encouraged the principal (the safecracker) before or during the crime
  • with the specific intent that the crime be completed.

As Case D shows, mere knowledge that the principal intended to use a person’s aid—particularly aid involving the sale of goods or services—to commit a crime does not show that the person intentionally aided the principal. But such intent can be inferred when a seller provides highly specialized goods or services (as seen in Case A), receives unusually large profits from the sale, or has an interest in the crime’s success beyond a mere sale.

Here, the surgeon removed fingerprints from a known safecracker at the surgeon’s usual hourly rate (Choice D). But since a procedure that allows persons to avoid detection is highly specialized, the surgeon’s intent to aid the safecracker in committing the burglary can be inferred—just as in Case A. Therefore, the surgeon should be convicted as an accomplice to the safecracker’s burglary on this authority.

(Choice B) Case B shows that a defendant can be convicted as a principal for encouraging an innocent agent to commit a crime. An innocent agent is someone who lacked the requisite mens rea (eg, intent) because he/she was tricked or forced into committing the crime. But since the safecracker intentionally committed burglary, this authority does not apply here.

(Choice C) Case C shows that a person is exempt from accomplice liability when (1) the aided crime requires at least two participants but (2) the criminal statute only imposes liability on one participant. But this exception does not apply here because burglary—unlike bribery or the sale of narcotics—only requires one participant.

📌 Educational Objective

An accomplice’s intent to aid the principal can be inferred when the accomplice (1) provides highly specialized goods or services, (2) receives unusually large profits from a sale, or (3) has some greater interest in the crime’s success.
questions.zh-question:
某个司法管辖区在主犯和共犯责任问题上，有以下判例法：

**判例A：** 被告，一名五金店老板，向几位顾客出售了一种能探测警用雷达并使超速者避免被发现的设备。当其中一台设备损坏，超速者被捕后，他承认自己经常超速，因为他知道该设备会提醒他附近有警用雷达。判决：被告构成超速的共犯（accomplice）。

**判例B：** 被告告诉一位朋友，他将一些音响设备存放在一个自助储物柜里。他给了朋友一把钥匙，让她去取设备并送到被告家。朋友照办，用钥匙从储物柜中取走了设备。事实上，这些设备属于被告的邻居，被告是在车道上捡到了邻居的储物柜钥匙。判决：被告构成入室盗窃（burglary）的主犯（principal）。

**判例C：** 一名市议会成员收受了被告的贿赂，以换取其在被告的区域规划变更（zoning variance）申请上的投票。一项法规禁止公职人员收受贿赂。判决：被告不构成市议会成员违反贿赂法规的共犯。

**判例D：** 被告，一名旅店老板，有时将房间租给妓女，他知道她们会利用这些房间从事性交易。他向妓女收取与旅店其他客人相同的价格。判决：被告不构成卖淫的共犯。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：帮助犯（accomplice liability）里，明知对方要犯罪还提供高度专业化服务（highly specialized services），能不能推定“我就是想帮他犯罪”。

三秒认题路径：

知道要犯罪 → 还在帮忙 → 服务很专业 → 意图可推定 → 选有罪

核心法律规则

帮助犯要成立，核心不是“他有没有亲手实施盗窃/ burglary”，而是他是否在犯罪前或犯罪中故意帮助或鼓励（intentionally aided or encouraged）主犯，并且特定目的（specific intent）是让犯罪完成。

考试里，单纯知道对方想犯罪还不够；但如果你提供的是高度专业化服务（highly specialized goods or services）、收了异常高额利润（unusually large profit），或对犯罪成功有更大利益，陪考人就能把“想帮忙”推出来。

核心判例： Case A 锁死本题：卖的是能帮助逃避侦查的专业工具/服务时，陪考人意图可以从交易本身推定出来。

思维导图

先看：他是自己去盗窃吗？
不是。 题干是医生替安全扒手去掉指纹，属于提供服务（service），不是自己爬进金库。
再看：有没有在犯罪前/中故意帮忙？
有迹象。 他明知对方是safecracker，还做能帮助躲避侦查的专业手术。
关键卡点：能不能推定 specific intent？
不能把 mere knowledge 当成意图？ 错；本题因服务高度专业化，可以推定意图。
对照 Case A：专业工具/服务 + 帮助逃避侦查 → 推定意图
结论： 选“有罪”，因为他不是路过知道，而是在提供会让犯罪更容易成功的专业帮助。
为什么不是别的 case？
Case B： 讲的是 innocent agent，别人被你骗着去犯案；这里安全扒手本人是故意犯罪，不是无辜工具。
Case C： 讲的是法条只罚一方、且行为本身要求至少两个人的特殊例外；burglary 不靠这个例外。
Case D： 只是普通收费卖淫房间的“照常交易”，和本题这种高度专业化的去指纹服务不同，不能拿来救被告。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他只是按正常时薪收费，哪有“帮犯罪”的主观恶意。

但考试真正问的是：这项服务是不是高度专业化（highly specialized）到足以让人推定他想帮对方完成犯罪，而不是只做一笔普通生意。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的去除指纹是高度专业化服务，且被告明知对方是安全扒手，意图可从交易本身推定，所以可按帮助犯定罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 无辜代理误套

✕ B: 把 innocent agent 搬错了，对方不是被你骗去犯罪。

❌ 法律适用 | 双人犯罪误套

✕ C: 把 two participants 的例外硬套到 burglary 上。

❌ 事实误判 | 普通交易偷换

✕ D: 只看 usual hourly rate，忽略了服务本身很专业、且专为逃避侦查服务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“提供什么帮助”，再问“这份帮助是否专业到足以推定帮凶意图”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“卖得越专业，越容易被推定想帮他犯罪；只说知道不够，得看帮助有没有把犯罪往前推。”

看到 帮助犯（accomplice liability） 时，先盯“专业服务 / 高额利润 / 更大利益”三件事；这三项一出现，意图就很容易被推出来。

reason.en: Ordinary payment can suggest the defendant was not charging a premium for criminal assistance.

reason.en: This matches the correct result because specialized assistance can support inferred intent to aid the burglary.
reason.zh: 这是正确结果，因为专业协助可支持推定帮助入室盗窃的故意。

reason.en: This is the best supporting authority because it involves specialized goods or services used to facilitate crime.
reason.zh: 这是最贴切的支持判例，因为涉及用于便利犯罪的专业商品或服务。

reason.en: The statutory-bribery exception does not apply because burglary does not require multiple participants.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:
CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.
CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.
CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.
CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes lent his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.
In this jurisdiction, conviction for statutory rape requires proof of the defendant's knowledge that the victim is underage. A high school student, who knew that a girl was underage, encouraged his friend, who was unaware of the girl's age, to have sex with the girl. The student has been charged with statutory rape.
Should the student be convicted or acquitted of this crime?

choices.A: Convicted on the authority of Case A.
choices.B: Convicted on the authority of Case B.
choices.C: Acquitted on the authority of Case C.
choices.D: Acquitted on the authority of Case D.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
Modern view Common law Definition Liability
Principal Principal
(first degree)		 Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act Target &
foreseeable
crimes
Accomplice Principal
(second degree)		 Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
before the fact*		 Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
after the fact		 Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction Independent
crime
*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

In this jurisdiction, statutory rape occurs when a person has sex with a victim (actus reus) with knowledge that the victim is underage (mens rea). And a conviction can stem from either:

  • principal liability – if the actus reus was committed by the defendant or, as evidenced in Case B, another who acted on the defendant's behalf but lacked the requisite mens rea (ie, an innocent agent) or
  • accomplice liability – if the defendant intentionally aided or encouraged another who had the requisite mens rea (ie, the principal) before or during a crime with the intent that the crime be completed.

Here, the student had the requisite mens rea since he knew that the girl was underage. But like the defendant in Case B, the student did not commit the actus reus—he encouraged his friend to do so. And since the friend lacked the mens rea necessary to commit statutory rape because he did not know that the girl was underage, he was an innocent agent (like the friend in Case B). Therefore, the student should be convicted of statutory rape as a principal—not an accomplice.

(Choices A, C, & D) Cases A, C, and D concern accomplice liability, which subjects the principal and accomplice to equal liability for a crime. But this theory of liability does not apply here because the friend lacked the necessary mens rea for statutory rape in this jurisdiction—ie, knowledge that the victim was underage. Therefore, the student cannot be liable as an accomplice to the friend's innocent act.

📌 Educational Objective

Principal liability is imposed when (1) the defendant possessed the requisite mens rea and (2) the actus reus was committed by the defendant or the defendant's innocent agent—ie, a person who lacked the mens rea required for the crime.

一个司法管辖区对主犯和从犯责任问题有以下判例法：

案例A：被告，一名五金店老板，向几位顾客出售了一种能探测警方雷达并使超速者避免被发现的设备。当其中一台设备发生故障，超速者被捕后，他承认自己经常超速，因为他确信该设备会提醒他附近有警方雷达。判决：被告构成超速罪的从犯 (accomplice)。

案例B：被告告诉一位朋友，他将一些音响设备存放在一个自助储物柜里。他给了朋友一把钥匙，并请她去取设备并送到被告家中。朋友照办了，并用钥匙从储物柜中取走了设备。事实上，这些设备属于被告的邻居，被告在车道上捡到了邻居的储物柜钥匙。判决：被告构成入室盗窃罪 (burglary) 的主犯 (principal)。

案例C：一名市议会成员接受了被告的贿赂 (bribe)，以换取他对被告区域规划豁免 (zoning variance) 申请的投票。一项成文法 (statute) 禁止公职人员收受贿赂。判决：被告不构成市议会成员违反贿赂法规的从犯 (accomplice)。

案例D：被告，一名旅店老板，有时会将房间借给妓女，他知道她们会利用这些房间从事卖淫活动。他对妓女收取的费用与旅店其他客人相同。判决：被告不构成卖淫罪的从犯 (accomplice)。

在该司法管辖区，法定强奸罪 (statutory rape) 的定罪要求证明被告知道受害人是未成年人 (underage)。一名高中生，明知一名女孩是未成年人，却鼓励他不知女孩年龄的朋友与该女孩发生性关系。该学生已被指控犯有法定强奸罪。

该学生应被判有罪 (convicted) 还是无罪释放 (acquitted)？

zh-choices.A: 依据案例A的判例，判有罪。
zh-choices.B: 依据案例B的判例，判有罪。
zh-choices.C: 依据案例C的判例，判无罪释放。
zh-choices.D: 依据案例D的判例，判无罪释放。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：主犯责任（principal liability）和共犯责任（accomplice liability）怎么分，关键看做事的人有没有构成该罪所需的mens rea。

三秒认题路径：

知晓未成年 → 自己有故意 → 友人不知情 → 友人是无辜代理人 → 选主犯

核心法律规则

如果题目说某罪要求特定mens rea，而被告自己知道关键事实、却让一个无辜代理人（innocent agent）去完成actus reus，考试上通常判被告是主犯（principal），不是共犯。共犯（accomplice）要求的是：帮助或鼓励的对象本身也得具备该罪所需的主观要件。这里友人不知道女孩未成年，所以他不能成立静止地被用来“转移”成共犯链条。

核心判例： Case B — 这个案子告诉你：用缺少必要主观要件的人去做动作，被告仍可能按主犯论。

思维导图

题干先问：这题是在考“我本人犯了罪”，还是“我帮了真正的主犯”？
第1步：被告自己知道女孩未成年吗？
是：主观要件已在被告这里满足。
第2步：真正做性行为的人知道女孩未成年吗？
否：他缺少 statutory rape 所需 mens rea，所以是 无辜代理人（innocent agent）。
第3步：谁完成了 actus reus？
是被告指使的友人完成动作，但法律上动作归到被告头上。
结论：被告按主犯责任（principal liability）定罪。
答案：B。别被“我只是叫别人做”骗成共犯。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他只是encouraged朋友去做，所以最多算共犯。

但考试真正问的是：完成犯罪动作的人有没有该罪所需的主观要件；这里友人不知道女孩未成年，所以他不是能把责任“接过去”的真正主犯。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 友人不知女孩未成年，所以友人是无辜代理人；被告自己知道未成年，还指使他完成行为，故按主犯定罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 共犯链套错

✕ A: 把帮助别人做事直接当成共犯，忽略了对方缺少必要主观要件。

❌ 法律适用 | 误套案例

✕ C: 这个案子讲的是对有主观要件的真正主犯提供帮助，不是本题这种无辜代理人情形。

❌ 事实误判 | 读漏关键事实

✕ D: 只盯着“他有知情”却漏看真正做事的人不知情，结论就会反掉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定谁有犯罪所需的 mens rea，再看 actus reus 是谁完成的；有无辜代理人时，先判主犯，不先判共犯。

考场速记

记忆口诀：知道规则的人指使不知情的人，通常先看主犯，不要急着套共犯。

本题速记：innocent agent 一出现，就先想“动作算到谁头上”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman promised to pay $10,000 to a hit man if he would kill her neighbor in any manner that could not be traced to her. The hit man bought a gun and watched the neighbor's house for an opportunity to shoot him. One evening, unaware of the hit man's presence, the neighbor tripped as he was walking toward his house, falling and hitting his head against the front steps. Believing that the neighbor was unconscious, the hit man ran over to him and shot him twice in the chest.
When the woman learned of the neighbor's death, she paid the hit man $10,000. A medical examiner determined that the neighbor was already dead when the hit man shot him.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness.
What is the most serious crime of which the woman properly could be convicted?

choices.A: Murder.
choices.B: Attempted murder.
choices.C: Conspiracy.
choices.D: Solicitation.

questions.explanation:
Inchoate crimes
Attempt
  • Specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of target crime
  • Merges with intended crime if completed
Conspiracy
  • Agreement entered with specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of agreement
  • No merger
Solicitation
  • Inducing or encouraging another to commit crime with specific intent that crime be committed, but solicited party need not agree
  • Merges with solicited crime if completed

Criminal liability is imposed equally upon:

  • principals – persons who commit a criminal act with the requisite mental state and
  • accomplices – persons who (1) intentionally aid or encourage the principal to commit a crime (2) with the specific intent that the principal complete that crime.

Both parties are liable for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the woman became an accomplice when she promised to pay the hit man $10,000 to commit a murder—ie, an unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought. But even though the man shot the neighbor twice in the chest, neither the man nor the woman can be convicted of murder because the fall (not the shooting) caused the neighbor's death (Choice A). However, they can be convicted of attempted murder since the shooting was an act committed in furtherance of the intended but unsuccessful murder.

(Choice C) The woman could be convicted of conspiracy—an agreement entered with the specific intent to commit a crime—even though the agreed-upon murder was not completed. But the conspiracy would also create accomplice liability for the more serious crime of attempted murder.

(Choice D) The woman committed solicitation (the least serious crime) when she requested that the hit man commit a murder with the specific intent that he do so. This request also established the woman's accomplice liability for attempted murder (a more serious crime).

📌 Educational Objective

The principal commits a criminal act with the requisite mental state, while the accomplice intentionally aids or encourages the principal with the specific intent that the principal complete that crime. Both are equally liable for the encouraged crime and its natural and probable consequences.

一名女子承诺向一名杀手支付10,000美元，条件是该杀手以任何无法追查到她的方式杀死她的邻居。杀手购买了一把枪并监视邻居的房屋，以寻找射杀他的机会。一天晚上，邻居在走向自己房屋时并未察觉到杀手的存在，不慎绊倒，头部撞在了门前台阶上。杀手以为邻居已失去知觉，便跑到他身边，向其胸部开了两枪。

当该女子得知邻居死亡后，她向杀手支付了10,000美元。法医鉴定，邻居在被杀手射杀时已经死亡。

以下罪行按严重程度降序排列。

该女子可被适当定罪的最严重罪行是什么？

zh-choices.A: 谋杀罪。
zh-choices.B: 谋杀未遂罪。
zh-choices.C: 共谋罪。
zh-choices.D: 教唆罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：出钱雇凶的人，最严重能不能按未遂杀人（attempted murder）定罪，而不是只停在教唆（solicitation）或共谋（conspiracy）。

三秒认题路径：

雇凶付钱 → 杀人故意 → 已有实行行为 → 死亡原因被切断 → 选未遂杀人

核心法律规则

未遂（attempt）考场意思：要有特定故意（specific intent），还要有朝目标罪前进的实行行为（overt act）。共谋（conspiracy）考场意思：双方先达成犯罪协议，再加一点实行行为；它不要求目标罪完成。教唆（solicitation）考场意思：只要你带着让对方去犯罪的故意去“叫人干”，即使对方还没点头，也已经成立。

如果本来想杀人，但最后没杀成，最能抓住你的通常是未遂杀人（attempted murder）；只要打了、追了、埋伏了，就已经不是“只是嘴上说说”了。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题锁定的是刑法中的未遂与共犯规则：雇凶者对未完成的杀人计划，最高可按未遂杀人追责。

思维导图

这不是“有没有杀死”的题，而是“雇凶后，最严重能定到哪一步”的题。
先看女人给了 $10,000，目的是让对方去杀邻居 → 她已进入教唆 / 共犯路径。
再看打手买枪、盯梢、开枪两次 → 已有朝杀人前进的实行行为（overt act）。
关键卡点验尸说邻居在枪击前已死 → 不能按既遂 murder，因为枪击没造成死亡。
剩下结论杀人故意 + 进一步实行行为 + 目标罪未完成 → Attempted murder。
顺手记住共谋、教唆都可能成立，但题目问“最严重”时，要继续往上找真正能落地的主罪责任。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：人都死了，当然该往murder上靠。
但考试真正问的是：死亡是不是由这次枪击造成，以及雇凶人对这次未完成的杀人计划能不能被拉到更重的未遂责任上。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 放在这题里就是：不是看“死没死”这个故事表面，而是看“最后那一下枪击有没有真的完成杀人”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里女人先付钱、打手再买枪并开枪，已经是朝杀人前进的实行行为；但死亡由先前摔倒造成，所以最严重只能落到未遂杀人（attempted murder）。

❌ 事实误判 | 误把致死原因当枪击

✕ A: 把shot him当成致死事实了。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看到协议没看升级

✕ C: 只盯着达成协议，漏掉后面已经推进到未遂杀人。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把最轻罪当最终答案

✕ D: 只认solicitation，忽略了雇凶后更重的未遂责任。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定最重可成立的实体罪，再往回看教唆、共谋只是下位标签，不要抢走未遂杀人的位置。

考场速记

记忆顺序：教唆（solicitation）看“叫人干”，共谋（conspiracy）看“先约好”，未遂（attempt）看“已经开始动手但没成”。这题最后要抓的是“动手了但没杀成”，所以答案到 attempted murder 为止。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A youth and two of his friends were members of a teenage street gang. While they were returning from a club late one evening, their car collided with a car driven by an elderly woman. After an argument, the youth attacked the elderly woman with his fists and beat her to death. The youth's two friends watched, and when they saw the woman fall to the ground, they urged him to flee.
The youth was eventually apprehended and tried for manslaughter, but the jury could not decide on a verdict.
If the youth's companions are subsequently tried as accomplices to manslaughter, should they be acquitted or convicted?

choices.A: Acquitted, because the youth was not convicted of the offense.
choices.B: Acquitted, because they did not assist or encourage the youth to commit the crime.
choices.C: Convicted, because they made no effort to intervene.
choices.D: Convicted, because they urged him to flee.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
Modern view Common law Definition Liability
Principal Principal
(first degree)		 Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act Target &
foreseeable
crimes
Accomplice Principal
(second degree)		 Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
before the fact*		 Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
after the fact		 Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction Independent
crime
*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

A person becomes an accomplice by (1) intentionally aiding or encouraging another (ie, the principal) before or during a crime (2) with the specific intent that the crime be completed. But mere presence at the scene of a crime does not amount to aid or encouragement and is therefore insufficient to make a person an accomplice.

Here, the friends were tried as accomplices to manslaughter after the youth beat the elderly woman to death in front of them. Although the friends urged the youth to flee after the beating was over, they did not aid or encourage the youth before or during this crime—they only watched. And since mere presence at a crime scene does not establish accomplice liability, the friends should be acquitted.

(Choice A) In most jurisdictions, an accomplice can be convicted even if the principal was never tried for, or convicted of, the aided/encouraged crime. So, the fact that the youth (principal) was never convicted does not immunize the friends. But they should be acquitted since they did not aid or encourage the youth's crime.

(Choice C) Criminal liability only arises from a failure to act (ie, omission) if a person had a legal duty to act and could have reasonably done so. Since the friends were mere bystanders with no duty to intervene on the woman's behalf, the fact that they made no effort to do so is irrelevant.

(Choice D) Persons who aid a principal after a crime has been completed (ie, accessories after the fact) are liable for a separate offense (eg, harboring a fugitive)—not the offense committed by the principal (eg, manslaughter). And merely urging the youth to flee is not sufficient post-crime assistance to establish such liability.

📌 Educational Objective

An accomplice intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime with the specific intent that the crime be completed. But mere presence at a crime scene does not make a person an accomplice.

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共犯（accomplice）是不是只因旁观、事后喊人逃跑，就要替杀人结果负责。

三秒认题路径：

旁观 → 未帮忙 → 只事后喊跑 → 不算共犯 → 选无罪

核心法律规则

这条规则怎么用在考场上

成为共犯（accomplice），必须在犯罪之前或进行中，有意帮助或鼓励主犯，而且还要有让犯罪完成的特定故意（specific intent）。mere presence，考场意思：只是站在旁边看，不等于帮忙。

本题里，两名朋友只是看着，真正的殴打发生时没有出手、没有鼓励、没有提供支持；等他打完后才叫他逃跑，这已经太晚了，不能把他们变成这次殴打的共犯。

核心判例： 这里不靠特殊例外，直接套用共犯基本规则：只在场不够，必须是犯罪前或犯罪中实际助力。

思维导图

先问：朋友有没有在犯罪前或进行中帮忙？
事实：他们只是站着看，直到人倒地后才喊他逃跑。
卡死点：事后喊跑 = post-crime assistance，不是共犯帮助。
再问：有没有 intent to aid，并且真的促成殴打？
没有：没有出手、没有劝打、没有协助工具或掩护。
结论：mere presence 不能自动升级成 accomplice。
最后落点：谁负责 manslaughter？
答案：主犯自己负责；朋友因没在犯罪时帮忙，不能因 accomplice 罪名定罪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他们明明看见人被打死，还叫他快跑，应该算帮凶。

但考试真正问的是：他们有没有在犯罪之前或进行中帮到这次殴打，而不是事后有没有做点事。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题换成共犯也是同一思路：事后补救不能回头变成事前助力。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是：两人只在旁边看，没有在行凶前或行凶中助攻，所以不构成共犯。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把主犯没定罪当成朋友自动无罪，是偷换共犯独立判断。

❌ 法律适用 | 不作为义务误套

✕ C: 把“没拦住”当成犯罪义务，但他们对受害人没有救助法定义务。

❌ 事实误判 | 事后帮助误读

✕ D: 只剩 flee 这一句，太晚了，顶多碰到事后帮助，不是本案共犯。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓时间点：只看犯罪前或进行中的助力，事后动作一律先排除。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先帮再犯才算共犯；只看不帮，事后才跑，通常都不够。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man and a woman agreed to engage in sexual intercourse at a particular hotel the following night. The man, who was the son of the woman's brother-in-law, rented the hotel room for their tryst, but the woman did not show up.
In the applicable jurisdiction, a statute provides that a person commits the offense of incest when such person engages in sexual intercourse with a person whom he or she knows he or she is related to either by blood or by marriage as aunt or nephew.
Can the woman and the man properly be charged with conspiracy to commit incest?

choices.A: No, because of Wharton's Rule.
choices.B: No, because the woman did not show up at the hotel.
choices.C: Yes, because each consented to engage in sexual intercourse.
choices.D: Yes, because the man rented a hotel room.

questions.explanation:
Wharton’s Rule

Only necessary parties
≠ Conspiracy
More than necessary parties
= Conspiracy

Most jurisdictions apply the unilateral approach to conspiracy.* Under this approach, a defendant can be convicted of conspiracy if:

  • the defendant entered into an agreement with another to commit a crime
  • the defendant specifically intended that the crime be committed and
  • at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.

But under Wharton’s Rule, if a crime requires two or more culpable parties (e.g., dueling, adultery, incest), there is no conspiracy unless more parties than are necessary to complete the crime agree to commit the crime.

Here, the man and the woman agreed to engage in sexual intercourse the following night. The man was the son of the woman’s brother-in-law (i.e., her nephew by marriage), so this act was criminalized under the incest statute. And the man rented a hotel room, which constituted an overt act. But incest requires two culpable parties. And this conspiracy to commit incest was completed by only the woman and the man, so Wharton’s Rule applies (Choice A). Therefore, the woman and the man cannot properly be charged with conspiracy to commit incest.

*Wharton’s Rule does not apply to jurisdictions that follow the Model Penal Code. However, it does apply to the remainder of jurisdictions—regardless of whether they apply the unilateral or bilateral approach to conspiracy.

(Choice B) It is irrelevant that the woman did not show up, as a unilateral conspiracy only requires that an overt act be performed by one of the co-conspirators. And here, the man rented a hotel room, satisfying the overt-act requirement. But Wharton’s Rule applies, so neither the man nor the woman can be convicted of conspiracy.

(Choice C) Consent is a defense only if the consent negates a required element of the crime (not seen here). However, the man and the woman cannot be convicted of conspiracy to commit incest because of Wharton’s Rule.

(Choice D) The man’s rental of a hotel room constituted an overt act, but it does not overcome Wharton’s Rule because only the two parties necessary to commit incest agreed to the crime.

📌 Educational Objective

Wharton’s Rule bars liability for conspiracy to commit a crime that requires at least two culpable parties if the conspiracy is completed by only the necessary number of parties.

该女子和该男子能否被恰当地指控犯有共谋乱伦罪（conspiracy to commit incest）？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为沃顿法则（Wharton's Rule）。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为该女子没有出现在酒店。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为他们各自同意发生性关系。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Inchoate offenses

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：两个人刚好是完成 乱伦（incest） 所必需的最低人数时，通常不能再叠加 共谋（conspiracy） 罪名，也就是 Wharton's Rule 怎么卡住起诉。

三秒认题路径：

两人合谋 → 必要共犯 → 仅最低人数 → Wharton's Rule → 不能共谋

核心法律规则

共谋（conspiracy） 一般看的是：先有协议，再有特定故意，最后还要有一个 overt act，考场意思：只要其中一人做了推进动作，通常就够了。

但 Wharton's Rule 说得更狠：如果某个罪名本身就必须靠两个或更多有罪主体才能完成，比如 incest、dueling、adultery，而合意的人数又没有超过完成该罪所必需的人数，就不能再另加 conspiracy。

这题里，发生性行为这件事本身就需要两个人；题干又只给了这两个人的合意，所以直接撞上 Wharton's Rule，考场意思：能不能再多算一个“合谋罪”，答案通常是不能。

核心判例： Wharton's Rule 本身就是本题控制规则；它锁定的结论是：只有完成该罪所必需的两人合意时，通常不成立共谋。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“只能由必要人数完成”的罪？
是 Wharton's Rule 启动：必要人数刚好够，不能再外挂 conspiracy
题干信号
两人约好去酒店 + 该州乱伦罪需要配偶/亲属双方参与
结果：协议人数 = 完成犯罪的必要人数
否
如果多出来第三人，或罪名不属于必要双人犯罪，才回到一般 conspiracy 分析：agreement + intent + overt act
这题的卡死点：
不是看有没有 overt act，而是看人数有没有超过完成罪名所必需的人数。
答案
选 A：不能因为这两个人就再加控 conspiracy to commit incest。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：男方已经租了酒店房间，女方也先同意了，说明 overt act 和协议都齐了，所以应该能判共谋。

但考试真正问的是：这个罪名是不是本来就只需要这两个人完成；如果是，就会被 Wharton's Rule 卡掉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同样要盯住法律结构，不要被“有人已经做了推进动作”这类细节带偏。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 只有两名必要参与者 正好满足乱伦完成所需人数，Wharton's Rule 直接挡住额外的共谋指控。

❌ 事实误判 | 缺席细节误看

✕ B: 把 did not show up 当成关键，但共谋不要求她亲自到场。

❌ 概念混淆 | 同意效力误判

✕ C: 把“同意”当成能救共谋的万能钥匙，其实这里卡的是 Wharton's Rule。

❌ 法律适用 | 推进行为误套

✕ D: 看到 rented a hotel room 就冲动认定成立，但 overt act 也救不了人数不够的共谋。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判断是不是必要双人犯罪，再看是否只是“刚好两人”，是的话直接启动 Wharton's Rule。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Wharton's Rule 先看“人数够不够”，如果犯罪本身就需要这两个人，通常就别再加 conspiracy；In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这句是程序法口诀，这题不用套，但要记住考试永远先找“例外卡口”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A babysitter, while working one night, noticed that her next-door neighbor had left his house but the door had not closed completely behind him. The babysitter said to the 11-year-old boy she was watching, "Let's play a game. You go next door and see if you can find my laptop, which I lent to my neighbor, and bring it over here." The babysitter knew that the neighbor had a laptop and the babysitter planned to keep the laptop for herself.
The boy thought the laptop belonged to the babysitter. He went next door, found the laptop, and carried it out the front door. At that moment, the neighbor returned home and discovered the boy in his front yard with the laptop. The boy explained the "game" he and the babysitter were playing. The neighbor then took back his laptop and called the police.
What is the most serious crime for which the babysitter can be convicted?

choices.A: No crime, because the boy did not commit any crime.
choices.B: Attempted larceny, because the babysitter never acquired possession of the laptop.
choices.C: Larceny as an accomplice to the boy.
choices.D: Larceny by the use of an innocent agent.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
(modern & majority approach)
Party Definition Liability
Principal
  • Commits criminal act with requisite mens rea or
  • Tricks or forces another (ie, innocent agent) to commit criminal act
 Liable for resulting crime
Accomplice
  • Aids or encourages principal before or during crime with intent that principal commit crime
 Liable to same extent as principal
Accessory
after the fact
  • Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction
 Liable for independent crime (not principal's)

Larceny occurs when there is a trespassory taking and carrying away of another's personal property (actus reus) with the specific intent to permanently deprive that person of the property (mens rea). A conviction can stem from either:

  • principal liability – when the actus reus is committed by the defendant OR a person acting on the defendant's behalf without the requisite mens rea (ie, innocent agent) or
  • accomplice liability – when the defendant intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime with the intent that the crime be completed (making both parties equally liable for the crime).

Here, the babysitter intended to steal the neighbor's laptop, but did not personally take it. Instead, she encouraged the boy to do so by prompting him to retrieve what he believed to be her laptop. His mistaken belief negated the necessary intent for larceny. Therefore, the boy did not commit larceny, and the babysitter cannot be convicted as his accomplice (Choices A & C). But the babysitter can still be convicted as a principal since she used the boy (an innocent agent) to steal the laptop.

(Choice B) Attempt occurs when a defendant (1) has the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) commits an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) does not complete it. Since the larceny was completed when the boy took the laptop on the babysitter's behalf, she will be convicted of the completed crime—not attempt.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant can be criminally liable if he/she (1) personally commits a crime or uses an innocent agent to do so (principal liability) or (2) intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime with the intent that the crime be completed (accomplice liability). But an accomplice is only liable to the same extent as the principal.

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Inchoate Crimes and Parties - Parties to a Crime

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：利用无辜工具人（innocent agent）实施盗窃时，行为人可以按正犯（principal）定罪，而不是只能算共犯（accomplice）。

三秒认题路径：

想偷东西 → 自己没拿 → 诱使小孩拿 → 小孩无盗窃故意 → 正犯定罪

核心法律规则

盗窃（larceny）需要非法取走并搬走（trespassory taking and carrying away）他人动产，并且有永久剥夺（intent to permanently deprive）的故意。考场意思：只要真正完成取走的人没有盗窃故意，命题人就会追问是不是有人把他当成了无辜工具人（innocent agent）。

正犯（principal）不一定非得亲手拿东西；如果是你指使、利用、哄骗别人替你完成犯罪动作，法律会把这次行为算到你头上。考场意思：你不能因为“我没亲手碰”就逃掉，principal liability 仍然成立。

共犯（accomplice）要求你是有意帮助真正的犯罪人去完成犯罪；如果那个“被你帮助的人”根本没形成犯罪故意，那就没有共犯可依附。考场意思：先看对方是不是在犯法，不是的话，就别硬套accomplice liability。

核心判例： 本题采用现代多数规则：利用无辜工具人（innocent agent）完成犯罪的人，按正犯处理；因此 babysitter 不是只算试图唆使，而是直接成立既遂盗窃。

思维导图

先看谁完成了“拿走”动作？
事实小孩把 laptop 拿出门，但他以为那是 babysitter 的东西。
法律关卡没有永久剥夺他人财物的故意，所以小孩不构成盗窃。
既然小孩不是盗窃人，babysitter 还能被定什么？
关键转折她是故意骗小孩替自己取走邻居的 laptop。
卡死点：她把无辜工具人当成自己的手在用，直接算正犯。
结论
答案不是 attempted larceny，也不是 accomplice；最重是 D 选项：larceny by the use of an innocent agent。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她自己没有亲手拿走 laptop，所以最多只是教唆，甚至只是未遂。

但考试真正问的是：谁在法律上完成了取走动作，而不是谁的手碰到了东西。

司法考试看的是「法律上谁完成了犯罪」，而不是「表面上谁先把东西拿在手里」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里 babysitter 故意让不知情的小孩替她把 laptop 拿走，小孩没有盗窃故意，所以她是用无辜工具人（innocent agent）完成既遂盗窃。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略无辜工具

✕ A: 以为小孩没犯罪，babysitter 也就自动没罪。

❌ 法律适用 | 把既遂说成未遂

✕ B: 把 attempted larceny 套进来，但她已经借小孩完成了取走。

❌ 概念混淆 | 正犯共犯倒置

✕ C: 误把“指使别人”当成只能算共犯，忘了她是借别人当手。

这题建议用什么方法？

先查“执行动作的人有没有故意”，再决定是共犯还是无辜工具人正犯。

考场速记

记住这句：故意借无辜人之手（innocent agent），就按正犯（principal）定，不要先想共犯或未遂。

reason.en: Shows the actor used by the babysitter to carry out the taking.
reason.zh: 表明保姆借助该未成年人实施取走行为。

keywords.text: The babysitter planned to keep the laptop for herself.

reason.en: Supplies the mens rea for larceny.
reason.zh: 提供盗窃罪所需的主观故意。

keywords.text: The boy thought the laptop belonged to the babysitter.

reason.en: Negates the boy's larcenous intent and supports innocent-agent liability.
reason.zh: 否定男孩的盗窃故意，支持无辜代理人责任。

keywords.text: carried it out the front door

reason.en: Shows the asportation element of larceny was completed.
reason.zh: 表明盗窃罪的取走要件已经完成。

reason.en: Invites the mistaken view that the babysitter escapes liability because the boy lacked mens rea.
reason.zh: 诱导误以为男孩无故意就导致保姆免责。

A.text: the boy did not commit any crime

reason.en: Focuses on the boy's innocence, which does not defeat principal liability through an innocent agent.
reason.zh: 强调男孩无罪，但这不否定通过无辜代理人成立的主犯责任。

reason.en: Mislabels a completed taking as only an attempt.
reason.zh: 把已完成的取走行为误写成仅仅未遂。

reason.en: Suggests the crime failed because the babysitter never physically held the laptop.
reason.zh: 暗示因为保姆未亲手控制电脑所以犯罪未完成。

C.text: Larceny as an accomplice to the boy

reason.en: Treats the boy as the principal even though his mistake negated larcenous intent.
reason.zh: 把男孩当作主犯，但其误信已否定盗窃故意。

D.text: Larceny by the use of an innocent agent

reason.en: States the correct basis for principal liability when another person is used to commit the taking without criminal intent.
reason.zh: 指出当他人无犯罪故意但被利用实施取走时，成立主犯责任的正确依据。

highlights.text: The babysitter planned to keep the laptop for herself.

reason.en: Identifies the babysitter's intent to steal.
reason.zh: 表明保姆具有盗窃意图。

highlights.text: The boy thought the laptop belonged to the babysitter.

reason.en: Shows the boy lacked the intent needed for larceny.
reason.zh: 说明男孩缺乏盗窃所需故意。

highlights.text: He went next door, found the laptop, and carried it out the front door.

reason.en: Supports completion of the larceny actus reus.
reason.zh: 支持盗窃行为要件已完成。

highlights.text: What is the most serious crime for which the babysitter can be convicted?

reason.en: Frames the task as selecting the highest supported completed offense.
reason.zh: 说明题目要求选择可成立的最高罪名。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Four men are being tried for conspiracy to commit a series of bank robberies. Nine successful bank robberies took place during the period of the charged conspiracy. Because the robbers wore masks and gloves and stole the bank surveillance tapes, no witnesses have been able to directly identify the robbers. Some circumstantial evidence ties each of the men to the overall conspiracy.
During cross-examination, a prosecution witness testified that one of the men was in jail on other charges during the last six robberies. That man's lawyer has moved for a judgment of acquittal at the close of the government's case.
Should the motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because a conspirator is not required to agree to all of the objectives of the conspiracy.
choices.B: No, because a conspirator need not be present at the commission of each crime conspired upon.
choices.C: Yes, provided that the man has complied with the rule requiring pretrial notice of alibi.
choices.D: Yes, regardless of compliance with the alibi rule, because the government is bound by exculpatory evidence elicited during its case-in-chief.

questions.explanation:
